text:
maya: Hey support — new customer 'Crescent Labs' finished onboarding but their API token is visible in the console under our internal project `staging-test` instead of the customer's project. They get 403 with `project_access_denied` when calling the API. Anyone seen provisioning route creds to the wrong project?

anna: Can you paste the org_id + expected project_id and a screenshot of the token row? Also want the exact error body from the API call.

maya: org_id: org-crest-009, expected project_id: proj-crest-01. Token row in console shows project_id: proj-internal-42. Here is the curl we ran and the response:```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}' 
# -> {"error":"project_access_denied","message":"token not authorized for project proj-crest-01"}```

louis: That curl actually proves the token is bound to proj-internal-42. Two possibilities: (1) provisioner picked a wrong project id during OIDC/claim binding; (2) token was created as a manual fallback into the internal pool. Do we have a provisioning-job log for that org?

maya: attaching the provisioner request id: prov-2026-09-02-8743. From the console audit: `provisioner: created_token token_id=tok-789 project=proj-internal-42 requested_project=proj-crest-01`. Looks like requested_project is correct but final project is wrong.

chris (eng-infra): Thanks — could be a race where the project binding step failed and we fell back to the internal project (we recently added that fallback for noisy edge cases). I'll check the provisioner logs for prov-2026-09-02-8743. In the meantime you can reassign the token to the correct project with the admin API:```bash
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer admin_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://admin.redwood.example/v1/tokens/tok-789 
  -d '{"project_id":"proj-crest-01"}'
# returns 200 and token.project_id should become proj-crest-01
```

support-jen: Escalating to eng-infra and flagging for a postmortem. Creating internal ticket RW-1268 and cc'ing customer success. @chris (eng-infra) please add rollback plan if this is part of a deployment.

deploy-bot: Ticket RW-1268 created by support-jen. Priority: P2. Linked: prov-2026-09-02-8743.

chris (eng-infra): Quick update — provisioner logs show a transient 500 from the project-sync service at the exact time of provisioning. Provisioner retried and hit fallback code path that routes tokens to `proj-internal-42`. I'm going to push a hotfix to remove fallback assignment and add a retry window.

maya: I patched the token via the admin API and the customer's calls now succeed (200). Sent screenshots to the customer.

anna: Nice. For postmortem notes: (1) identify why project-sync returned a 500; (2) remove silent fallback or make it explicit in UI/email; (3) add a telemetry alert when token.project_id != requested_project for >=1 failed binds.

chris (eng-infra): Agreed. I'll own the fix and follow up in RW-1268 with the changelist. ETA for deploy: 24h.

support-jen: Closing this slack thread — customer notified and workaround applied. Will keep RW-1268 open until fix out. :white_check_mark:
